subject: Discovery: Integration adapter options & function-calling patterns
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kate Liu <kate@clearsight.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Recap + options: adapter approach for function/tool calling and rerankers

Hi Kate / Charles —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate. Short version: ClearSight is evaluating an integration that will use Redwood for generation + a reranker/embeddings pipeline, and you want recommendations on SDK setup, auth, request routing, and safe function/tool calling patterns.

Notes from the call (high level):
- Primary workflows: 1) interactive agent UI (agents call internal tools: search, ticket-create, pricing lookup), 2) batch rerank for candidate documents (embedding-based followed by lightweight model reranker).
- Nonfunctional constraints: sub-200ms soft-latency for UI actions, strict PII controls, vendor isolation for PCI-adjacent requests.
- Current infra: microservices on AWS (EKS), company auth via Okta (OIDC), internal API gateway.

Attachments: I attached a short adapter-patterns draft and a one-page SOW clarification.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share two architecture options (low-effort: Redwood SDK + sidecar adapters; higher-effort: dedicated adapter microservice with shared routing) — Karthik/Neha to propose patterns.
2) Match on auth model (token exchange, mTLS, or API Key rotation via KMS).
3) Walkthrough of tool definition surface and recommended error-handling strategies (timeouts, retries, fallbacks).
4) Schedule a 30-min technical working session next week to lock the integration scope.

Questions for you:
- Which agent/tool calls must be synchronous vs allowed to be async? (e.g., ticket-create can be async with callback; pricing lookup needs sync).
- For rerank: do you prefer embedding store in your VPC or hosted by Redwood?

I’ll loop in Karthik and Neha to sketch the two architecture options and a short decision matrix.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: sow-clarify.docx (45 KB, docx)

Cc: Charles Huang <charles@clearsight.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + options: adapter approach for function/tool calling and rerankers

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Sync vs async: pricing lookup must be sync (UI needs immediate response). Ticket-create and long-running enrichments can be async.
- PII: we must keep raw documents within our VPC; embeddings can be computed in Redwood if we establish a private VPC peering and KMS key policy.
- Our security team prefers mTLS for service-to-service calls if possible, otherwise token exchange via Okta.

We’d like to see the two architecture options and a recommended fallbacks matrix for tool failures (e.g., if search times out, fall back to cached candidates; if reranker fails, present generation output with confidence flag).

Available for a deep dive next Wed morning ET.

—Kate
Head of Product | ClearSight AI
kate@clearsight.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Recap + options: adapter approach for function/tool calling and rerankers

Karthik / Neha —

Forwarding ClearSight's clarifications. They confirmed: pricing lookup needs to be sync; ticket-create can be async; prefer mTLS or Okta token exchange; embeddings ideally in their VPC but open to hosted if we set up peering + KMS.

Please draft:
- Option A (fast): Redwood SDK + in-process adapter with per-route routing rules. Pros: quick to ship, lower infra changes for ClearSight. Cons: harder to enforce strict mTLS and VPC separation.
- Option B (robust): Dedicated adapter microservice in ClearSight VPC that mediates tool calls + does auth exchange, with Redwood routes to either hosted model endpoints or private connectors. Pros: strong isolation, flexible auth, easier audit/logging. Cons: more infra work.

Specifically enumerate for each option:
- SDK setup steps (language targets, sample code block),
- Recommended auth pattern (mTLS instructions vs token exchange flow),
- Routing policy suggestions (latency vs cost, model-variant fallback),
- Tool/function calling guidance: tool definitions surface (name, input schema, output schema, permission scope), parallel tool orchestration patterns, and error-handling best practices (timeouts, retries, idempotency, degrade-to-model).

Also propose a short decision matrix for embeddings: hosted vs VPC-hosted (cost, latency, security).

I’ll consolidate and send to Kate with a 30-min slot for Wed morning.

Thanks —
Lauren

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + options: adapter approach for function/tool calling and rerankers

Lauren / Neha —

Below are concise options and concrete recommendations we can send to ClearSight tomorrow. I focused on practical patterns they can implement quickly and an escalation path for higher isolation.

Option A — SDK + lightweight adapter (recommended for PoC)
- SDK setup: use Redwood Node or Python SDK; sample initialization: `RedwoodClient(api_key=ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'], region='us')` with SDK-provided helpers for streaming and structured output validation.
- Auth: token exchange pattern (Okta -> short-lived Redwood token) using OAuth2 client credentials + token exchange. Provide a small helper lib that calls Okta and caches tokens in memory with TTL.
- Routing: per-endpoint routing table (pricing->low-latency endpoint, embeddings->batch endpoint). Use header hints (x-rdw-priority) to pick model variant.
- Tool defs: keep them explicit JSON schemas. Example tool surface: `{name: 'pricingLookup', schema_in: {sku:string, qty:int}, schema_out: {price:float, currency:string}, permissions: ['pricing:read']}`.
- Parallel tools: fan-out pattern with scatter/gather for independent calls (search + enrichment run in parallel), then merge by keys. Use correlation IDs and a short 300ms window for UI-critical calls.
- Error handling: prefer fast failover — for sync calls set 150ms internal timeout, 2 retries with exponential backoff; on final failure, fall back to cache or model-only generation with a confidence_tag. Ensure idempotency keys for ticket-create.

Option B — Dedicated adapter microservice (recommended for production with strict isolation)
- SDK setup: same; the adapter owns calling Redwood and internal services. Adapter runs in their VPC and holds mTLS certs.
- Auth: mTLS between adapter <-> ClearSight services; adapter authenticates to Redwood via short-lived tokens minted by ClearSight KMS. This keeps raw data inside the customer boundary.
- Routing: router inside adapter uses policy engine (latency vs cost vs model-quality), can call Redwood private endpoints or hosted endpoints depending on SLA.
- Tool defs: register tool capabilities in a central registry (name, input/output schema, rate_limits, required_permissions). Adapter enforces permissions via token scopes.
- Parallel tools: orchestrate with a small concurrency controller. For UI-critical parallel calls, prefer optimistic aggregation: return best-effort partials to the front end and update once completion arrives.
- Error handling: heavier observability: structured traces, ability to replay failed calls, circuit-breakers per tool. Include graceful degradation policies: degrade_to_cached_candidates, degrade_to_model, or escalate.

Reranker / Embeddings decision matrix
- Hosted embeddings (Redwood-hosted): pros — simpler ops, lower engineering cost; cons — network egress / compliance concerns.
- VPC-hosted store: pros — full data control, local low-latency queries; cons — more ops and cost.

Implementation notes (common):
- Structured outputs: enforce JSON schema and run a lightweight validator before persisting or calling downstream tools. Reject or sanitize fields that contain PII per policy.
- Logging: redact PII at capture point; store full traces only in customer-controlled storage if requested.
- Retries: make all retries idempotent; ticket-create should use idempotency token returned to client.

I can turn this into a one-page decision doc + sample code snippets. Recommend we offer a 60-minute tech session to walk the adapter flow and auth exchange.

—Karthik
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
